nodes.content: Develop streaming speech recognition that handles temporarily ambiguous speech accurately while committing words irreversibly with low latency.
requirements: Achieve word error rate within 5% relative of an equally trained revisable streaming baseline.
Keep 95th-percentile word-end-to-commit latency below 800 milliseconds, with zero revisions after commitment.

nodes.content: Buffer competing transducer hypotheses; commit consensus prefixes irreversibly, forcing minimum-risk choices 700 ms after estimated word ends.
What beam posterior-mass threshold prevents premature homophone commits without exceeding the 700-ms forced-decision window?
A 0.95 consensus-mass threshold limits homophone-rich WER increase to 5% relative to revisable decoding, with p95 latency <800 ms.
Sweep 0.90, 0.95, and 0.99 consensus thresholds on homophone-enriched LibriSpeech; compare WER and p95 latency with revisable decoding.
Decode homophone-enriched LibriSpeech at 0.90, 0.95, 0.99 and revisable baseline; record WER, p95 word-end-to-commit latency, and postcommit revisions.
At 0.95, WER was 11.0% versus revisable 10.2% (+7.8% relative); p95 latency was 742 ms, with zero revisions.
With 700-ms forced commits, adaptive consensus-mass thresholds (0.99 for homophones, 0.90 otherwise) yield WER ≤10.7% and p95 latency <800 ms.
Using 0.95-run errors, implement online homophone flagging; test 0.99/0.90 thresholds on held-out LibriSpeech for WER, p95 latency, and revisions.
Held-out LibriSpeech: adaptive WER 10.6% versus revisable 10.2% (+3.9% relative); p95 latency 761 ms; zero postcommit revisions.
After adaptive decoding meets aggregate targets, stratify the 0.90/0.95/0.99 LibriSpeech sweep by ambiguity duration; compare subgroup WER and p95 latency.
Ambiguity-duration audit with per-bin WER and p95 commit latency for fixed thresholds, adaptive decoding, and the revisable baseline.
For ambiguities exceeding 500 ms, does adaptive decoding retain ≤5% relative WER increase and sub-800-ms p95 commit latency?
Use the duration audit to gate adaptive-decoder release on >500-ms subgroup compliance; aggregate WER and latency already meet targets.
Distill a 400-ms future-context teacher into a causal transducer; commit at 2% estimated error risk or a 700-ms deadline.
Distill the 400-ms teacher into a causal transducer; calibrate commit risk and compare held-out WER, p95 latency, and revisions.
Use audit-defined >500-ms ambiguity bins to oversample 400-ms-teacher distillation examples; calibrate causal-student 2%-risk commits before 700 ms.
Causal transducer checkpoint with audit-bin-weighted teacher distillation, calibrated 2%-risk commit scores, and a hard 700-ms commit deadline.
Benchmark distilled checkpoint against equally trained revisable decoding on held-out LibriSpeech; measure WER, p95 commit latency, revisions, and long-ambiguity WER.
Held-out LibriSpeech: distilled WER 11.1% versus revisable 10.2% (+8.8% relative); p95 latency 704 ms; zero revisions.
Are the distilled model’s excess errors concentrated in >500-ms ambiguity bins or in miscalibrated 2%-risk early commits?
Stratify distilled-checkpoint errors by ambiguity duration and commit timing; compare predicted versus observed error for early 2%-risk commits.
Replay checkpoint outputs; tabulate excess substitutions by >500-ms ambiguity and observed errors among early commits scored below 2% risk.
Early commits scored below 2% risk had 1.7% observed error; 73% of excess substitutions arose at 700-ms deadlines.
Can ambiguity-aware rescoring at 700-ms deadlines lower WER to ≤10.7% while keeping p95 commit latency below 800 ms?
Homophone-aware rescoring of deadline beam candidates reduces WER to ≤10.7% while preserving p95 latency <800 ms and zero revisions.
Using the 11.1%-WER checkpoint and deadline-error audit, rescore homophone beam candidates; measure WER, p95 latency, and revisions.
Homophone-aware rescoring cut WER from 11.1% to 10.6%; p95 commit latency was 746 ms, with zero revisions.
Adopt deadline-only homophone rescoring: WER fell from 11.1% to 10.6%, with 746-ms p95 latency and zero revisions.
Fine-tune a causal transducer with contrastive homophone minimal-pair loss; trigger irreversible commits using calibrated word-level error estimates.
Mine homophone minimal pairs, contrastively fine-tune the causal transducer, calibrate 700-ms commits, then benchmark WER and p95 latency.
Use audit-defined ambiguity bins to mine homophone minimal pairs and contrastively fine-tune the causal transducer on long-ambiguity examples.
Minimal-pair fine-tuned transducer checkpoint and labeled homophone-pair corpus, tagged by >500-ms ambiguity duration.
Calibrate checkpoint commit-risk scores, then benchmark irreversible decoding against equally trained revisable decoding on held-out LibriSpeech WER and p95 latency.
Minimal-pair checkpoint achieved 10.5% WER versus revisable 10.2% (+2.9% relative), 774-ms p95 commit latency, and zero revisions.
Train an alignment-supervised ambiguity-resolution predictor; commit stable prefixes immediately and defer uncertain words until resolution or 700 ms.
Can alignment-supervised resolution predictions identify words safely committable before 700 ms without increasing WER beyond 10.7%?
Alignment-supervised resolution gating commits at least 30% of words within 400 ms of word end while maintaining WER ≤10.7%.
Train alignment-supervised resolution gate with 700-ms deadline; measure held-out LibriSpeech ≤400-ms commit share, WER, p95 latency, and revisions.
Resolution gate committed 38% within 400 ms, but WER was 11.0% versus revisable 10.2%; p95 latency 753 ms, zero revisions.
Tune resolution-gate confidence on validation data; test ≥30% ≤400-ms commits, WER ≤10.7%, and p95 latency <800 ms.
Using the 11.0%-WER gate, sweep confidence cutoffs; retest held-out ≤400-ms commit share, WER, p95 latency, and revisions.
Tighter gate confidence yielded 32% commits within 400 ms, 10.6% WER versus 10.2% revisable, 779-ms p95 latency, zero revisions.
Does tightened resolution gating preserve ≤5% relative WER increase and sub-800-ms p95 latency under 10-dB babble noise?
Add 10-dB babble to held-out LibriSpeech; compare tightened gating with an equally trained revisable baseline on WER and p95 latency.
Under 10-dB LibriSpeech babble, benchmark original and tightened gates against revisable decoding for WER, p95 latency, and revisions.
10-dB babble robustness report comparing original gate, tightened gate, and revisable baseline on WER, p95 latency, and revisions.
Adopt tightened gating for clean speech (10.6% versus 11.0% WER); condition babble rollout on the robustness report meeting both targets.
Use a calibrated conformal prediction set over next-word candidates; commit only singleton sets, with minimum-risk fallback at 700 ms.
Calibrate 98% conformal word sets on validation speech; benchmark singleton commits against revisable decoding for WER and p95 latency.
Using the minimal-pair checkpoint and babble report, stratify 98%-coverage conformal calibration; compare singleton-commit WER and p95 latency against revisable decoding.
Stratified conformal calibrator with clean/babble word-set thresholds, singleton-commit decoder, and held-out WER and p95-latency tables.
Replay the singleton-commit decoder on independent clean/babble LibriSpeech; measure conformal coverage, WER versus revisable decoding, p95 latency, and revisions.
Independent clean/babble: WER 10.6/18.7% versus revisable 10.2/18.0%; coverage 98.1%, worst-case p95 latency 787 ms, zero revisions.
Will 98% conformal coverage persist for rare homophones while keeping their p95 commit latency below 800 ms?
Rare homophones retain ≥98% conformal coverage and <800-ms p95 commit latency under the stratified singleton-commit decoder.
Audit rare homophones in independent clean/babble outputs using the stratified calibrator; measure conformal coverage and p95 commit latency.
Rare-homophone audit found 98.2% conformal coverage and 792-ms p95 commit latency across clean/babble speech.
Adopt stratified conformal commits for clean/babble rollout over clean-only gating: WER and latency targets hold, with ≥98% rare-homophone coverage.
